A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SATQuest and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The retained content can be matched despite reformatting, appendix renumbering, and substantial additions in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of nine LLMs, GRPO fine-tuning experiments with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, and supporting case studies and analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical study and adds a hallucination audit, 14B-model fine-tuning experiments, and evaluations on external mathematics benchmarks.

M1.justification: The CNF generator, PySAT verification, binary-string outputs, and GRPO objective and rewards remain unchanged. The new narrative-conversion pseudocode documents transformations already illustrated in v1. The 14B and mixed-format trials reuse this method; Algorithm 1's counter-name correction does not change its intended procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix J adds actual evaluations on AIME2024 and DeepMind Mathematics, extending coverage from SATQuest's satisfiability tasks to broader mathematical reasoning. The original CNF datasets, five SAT task types, and four question formats are retained.

E2.justification: Tables 7-8 introduce joint SATSP-Math/Story GRPO training as a comparison variant alongside the single-format variants. The original nine-model benchmark comparison is retained. Claude-Sonnet-4.5 participates as an audit judge, not as a competing reasoning baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds 14B-model and mixed-format training experiments and specifies pass@4 for AIME2024. Appendix I introduces an audit using 20 selected CNF pairs, four Math tasks per pair, three reasoning models, Claude-Sonnet-4.5 labels, and 10% human checking. These are added protocols; the original 7B training and benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix I adds a systematic, multi-label failure analysis by task and solver complexity, extending v1's qualitative hallucination discussion. Appendix J tests whether cross-format difficulties persist at 14B and compares mixed-format training with single-format training. The original DIMACS case studies and generalization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly reports no confidence intervals or significance tests. v2 adds mean and standard-deviation bands to Figure 5, reports mean ± standard deviation over eight runs in Table 7, and identifies Figure 4 as single-run. Table 8 also includes ± values, without defining them locally. This does not establish that the retained experiments were rerun.

E6.justification: Tables 5-8 add hallucination rates, 14B fine-tuning results, and external-benchmark scores. For example, Table 7 reports SATSP-Math scores of 12.86 before and 70.80 after Math fine-tuning; Table 8 reports AIME2024 scores of 24.17 for the baseline, 25.83 after Math training, and 20.84 after Story training. These are new 14B comparisons. Original benchmark values in Figures 2, 4, 7, and 8 are retained.

T1.justification: The five SAT-task definitions remain mathematically equivalent. Explicit clause notation and the reformulated MCS/MUS conditions clarify existing definitions. The added narrative explanation introduces no new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical result.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a controllable CNF-based verifier for evaluation and reinforcement fine-tuning, with limited cross-format transfer. v2's introduction explicitly foregrounds complexity-associated hallucination and asymmetric cross-task transfer within its contribution statements, refining the earlier broader evaluation claims.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands limitations concerning synthetic English narratives, propositional scope, restricted instance sizes, and untested paraphrasing and training alternatives. It narrows the claimed correlation with other benchmarks to broadly consistent rankings. Conversely, Appendix J adds stronger interpretations about general mathematical improvement and intrinsic RFT limitations that exceed what its comparisons establish.

D1.justification: v2 adds narrative-conversion pseudocode, worked prompts, implementation and demonstration pointers, and an explicit zero-shot/no-tool description. It states that audit scripts, outputs, and judge logs are released. Original API identifiers, hyperparameters, hardware, and training times are retained; removing the checklist also removes the Weave recording disclosure.

R1.justification: v2 removes the citations to PySAT by Ignatiev et al. (2018) and Tulu 3 by Lambert et al. (2025). Section 5 otherwise retains substantially the same related-work comparisons and positioning. Shortened author lists and reordered references are bibliographic presentation changes.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. The combined summary and limitations becomes a conclusion plus a structured limitations and future-work discussion; terminology is standardized around the instance dimension. The appendix organization expands, acknowledgments are added, and the submission checklist is removed, although much technical prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adopts two-column layout, redraws the pipeline, rotates the overall-accuracy chart, and reorganizes complexity plots and heatmap panels and columns. It adds a generalization-summary table, four new results tables, and uncertainty bands in Figure 5. Figure 3's revised caption misidentifies the plotted left and right axes.

improvement.justification: The audit, larger-model experiments, uncertainty reporting, and clearer documentation strengthen v2's empirical support and transparency. The net gain is limited by overinterpretation: Appendix J claims consistent external improvement despite Table 8's AIME2024 decline from 24.17 to 20.84 after Story training, and attributes cross-format failure to RFT without excluding capacity or dataset effects. These weaknesses temper the benefits of the added evidence.
